title: OneShot with fadein breaks animation
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1]
v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]
v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.11 GiB memory

### Issue description

When animating with `AnimationTree` (`BlendTree` as root), if `OneShot` has `fadein` or `fadeout` with certain timings, it breaks certain rotation animations. For example, an attack animation where a hand rotates significantly starts to skip quite a lot and visibly jumps. The problem disappears if `fadein` and `fadeout` of the `OneShot` animation node are zero or changed to other timings. With the example animation, the issue is clearly visible with 1s `fadein`.

My guess is it's somehow related to interpolation of positions but even if quaternion takes the shorter route and rotates in the "wrong" direction, it doesn't explain why the animation visibly jumps to a different position.

Maybe I'm misunderstanding something about the animation system in Godot. Please take a look at the example.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e119123-cce3-4812-a05c-a6a7860fdb55)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the example project.
2. Run the main scene (`test.tscn`).
3. Press Space to trigger the `OneShot`.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[animation_glitch_example.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23566286/animation_glitch_example.zip)
